notes.title: LOADOUT SYSTEM
notes.notes:
[b]Attention Commanders,[/b]

A few months ago, we introduced the Loadout System as a new layer of strategy and customization. While the core idea was received with excitement, we also heard your concerns and suggestions loud and clear. Over the past months, we’ve had one-on-one discussions with many of you, collaborated closely with veteran players, and worked hand-in-hand with our dev team to refine the system.

Thanks to your valuable insights, we’ve made several meaningful changes that bring the feature more in line with how you want to play. Here’s what’s new:

[b]Key Changes and Improvements:[/b]
[list][*]
Pharmaceuticals are no longer used to provide attack boosts.
[/*][*]
Pharmaceuticals are now focused on healing and defense boosts, better supporting unit sustainability.
[/*][*]
A Hospital is now needed to produce pharmaceuticals, replacing the Secret Lab.
[/*][*]
Healing remains time-based.
[/*][/list]
Attack and defense boosts are now combat round-based, they activate only during actual engagements and do not expire over time. This change was made to address feedback about hesitance to use time-limited boosts.

[b]Expanded Munitions System:[/b]
We added Ground, Sea, and Air Munitions with tailored enhancements for each. This highly requested feature gives you a powerful attack boost.

[b]Looking Ahead[/b]
This is just the next step, not the final one. We are cautiously expanding and refining this system, and your feedback has been instrumental in shaping its direction. Please keep sharing your ideas and experiences as they matter a lot to us!

This updated system is now available on all platforms.

A big thank you to everyone who took the time to test, critique, and improve this feature with us. Your dedication to helping us build the best version of World War 3 is truly appreciated.

See you on the battlefield!

notes.title: A New Era Begins - Uniting Our Games & Studios
notes.notes:
[b]A New Era Begins - Uniting Our Games & Studios[/b] 
Big changes are on the horizon, and we’re excited to share them with you first! After years of collaboration, Bytro and Dorado are officially becoming one unified company. This marks a new era—a fresh start with a new look, new aspirations, and bold ideas for the future.

 We are aligning our strengths, refining our goals, and setting the stage for even greater strategy gaming experiences. This transformation is about more than just a name; it’s about reinforcing our commitment to our players and ensuring that our games continue to evolve while staying true to their roots.

[previewyoutube=yrwuWk4GSwg;full][/previewyoutube]

 But that’s just the beginning.

 [b]A Unified Franchise: Welcome to the Supremacy Era[/b]

 With our studios coming together, we are also aligning our games under one unified [b]Supremacy[/b] franchise. [b]Supremacy 1914, Call of War, and Conflict of Nations[/b] will now carry the Supremacy name—creating a recognizable brand that strengthens all of our strategy games while keeping each title’s unique identity intact.

 Here’s what this means for you:

 [b]Same core gameplay & mechanics[/b] – No fundamental changes to how your favorite games play.
 [b]No progress loss[/b] – Everything you’ve earned stays with you.
 [b]More content & improvements[/b] – A stronger foundation for future updates and community support.

 [b]Rebranding: A New Look, Same Great Games[/b]

 As part of this evolution, the games will receive a branding update:
[list][*][b]Supremacy 1914[/b] – Stays the same![/*][*][b]Call of War[/b] – Will transition to [b]Supremacy: Call of War 1942[/b].[/*][*][b]Conflict of Nations[/b] – Will become [b]Supremacy: World War 3[/b].[/*][/list]
 This helps players instantly recognize the connections between our games while preserving their distinct gameplay and settings. Think of it like other popular game franchises—different titles, but all part of the same legendary franchise.

 [b]What’s Next?[/b]

 [b]New Studio Name[/b] – A single name to represent our combined strength.
 [b]Unified Login[/b] – Work is underway to streamline access across all games.
 [b]Shared Community[/b] – We’ll transition to a [b]single Supremacy Discord server[/b] for a stronger, more connected player base.
 [b]More Games in the Future?[/b] – While nothing is official yet, this new structure paves the way for future expansions.

 [b]Your Role in This Evolution[/b]

 We know change can bring questions, and we’re here to answer them. This is a [b]collaborative journey[/b], and your feedback is key to making this transition smooth. Join the discussion, share your thoughts, and let’s move forward together.

 More updates will follow soon—[b]stay tuned![/b]

notes.title: A Dying World
notes.notes:
[b]Attention Commanders![/b]

[b]A Dying World is upon us!
Running from April 23rd to August 18th [/b]

As the climate crisis escalates, the world is on the brink of collapse. Resources have dwindled, nations have fractured or formed uneasy alliances, and mass migration towards domed cities has left once thriving metropolises abandoned. But even in the face of environmental catastrophe, one thing remains constant …..war.

[b]Elite Armored Fighting Vehicle (Elite AFV)[/b]
An advanced version of the traditional Armored Fighting Vehicle, the Elite AFV enhances naval combat with its unique abilities:

Transforms into an Amphibious Assault Ship when navigating water. The Elite AFV is a formidable unit designed for storming cities with amphibious precision. Carried in its own Heavy Transport Ship, it boasts minor combat capabilities at sea, ensuring it remains a self-sustaining force in coastal operations.

[b]Sea Mines[/b]
Sea Mines are a new defensive tool designed to disrupt enemy naval movements and fortify your maritime borders.

[list]
[*] [b]Stealthy & Single-Use:[/b] Sea Mines remain hidden until triggered.
[*] [b]Heavy Damage: [/b]Once detonated, they deal devastating damage to enemy ships.
[*] [b]Limited Lifespan:[/b] They exist for a set duration before deactivating.
[*] [b]Deployable by Select Units:[/b] Mines can be placed strategically in shallow waters.
[/list]

[b]Flagship Scenario: The Aftermath of Rising Tides[/b]
A sequel to Rising Tides, this new scenario introduces river terrain, significantly altering the strategic landscape:

[list]
[*] [b]Rivers Split Nations:[/b] Some countries will now be separated by rivers, creating new tactical challenges.
[*] [b]Flooded Lowlands:[/b] Parts of the world are now submerged, emphasizing naval and amphibious warfare.
[*] [b]Resource Scarcity: [/b]No additional resource production from provinces, annexing cities is now crucial.
[*] [b]Damaged Domed Cities:[/b] Cities start with damaged infrastructure, reflecting the recent chaos.
[/list]
[b]Rivers and Their Effects:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Impassable for[/b]: Destroyers, Cruisers, Aircraft Carriers, Submarines, and Helicarriers.
[/list]

[b]Season Missions[/b]
A total of [b]6 missions[/b], each containing 4-6 steps, will guide you through the mechanics of the season:

[olist]
[*] [b]Introduction to the New Scenario:[/b] Learn how to navigate the new war-torn world.
[*] [b]Master the Elite AFV:[/b] Utilize this powerful amphibious unit to its full potential.
[*] [b]Counter the Elite AFV:[/b] Develop strategies to neutralize this formidable threat.
[*] [b]Build Your Naval Fleet: [/b]Strengthen your forces for upcoming sea battles.
[*] [b]Naval Warfare Tactics:[/b] Destroy enemy fleets while preserving your own.
[*] [b]Submarine Warfare:[/b] Deploy your Submarine Officer to hunt and eliminate enemy officers.
[/olist]

A new era of war is here. Are you ready to adapt and survive in A Dying World?
See you on the battlefield, Commander!

notes.title: Infrastructure Upgrade
notes.notes:
[b]++++UPDATE++++

[/b]

[b]Upcoming Infrastructure Upgrade - [/b][b]Improving Stability & Creative Freedom[/b]
Over the next few months, we are making major improvements to our infrastructure. Currently, our Call of War 1942, Conflict of Nations, Iron Order 1919, and Supremacy 1914 share a common infrastructure, meaning updates or issues in one title can impact others. To ensure stronger uptime, greater stability, and more creative flexibility for each game’s development, we are moving each game to its own dedicated infrastructure.

[b]Why This Matters[/b]
Dorado and Bytro are committed to continuously improving our technology to provide a smooth and reliable experience. This separation will not only [b]reduce cross-game disruptions but also allow our teams to push the boundaries of innovation without compromising performance.[/b]
[b]
What to Expect[/b]
[b]Planned Downtime[/b] - Each game will experience a temporary downtime during its transition.
We estimate [b]1-2 hours for the game that is split from the shared infrastructure[/b], with matchmaking and game rounds briefly unavailable.
We estimate [b]a few minutes for games that remain on the shared infrastructure[/b] 
We will provide more exact times ahead of each split.
[b]
Estimated Timeline:[/b]

[b]Iron Order 1919[/b] – February
[b]Call of War 1942[/b] – April
[b]Conflict of Nations[/b] – May–June
[b]Supremacy 1914[/b] – June–July

This is a [b]massive project[/b], and we appreciate your patience as we work to create a stronger and more independent infrastructure for each game. Stay tuned for further updates as we approach each transition.

Thank you for your support!
[b]Your Conflict of Nations Team[/b]

notes.title: New ELO System
notes.notes:
[b]++++UPDATE++++[/b]

[b]Commanders,[/b]

The wait is over! The much-anticipated [b]new ELO system[/b] is officially live and ready to transform the competitive landscape for alliances worldwide. This overhaul ensures a more accurate, fair, and dynamic ranking system that better reflects the true skill and activity of alliances.

[i]Here’s a recap of what’s now in effect:[/i]

[b]Game History Recalculation[/b]

The updated ELO system has retroactively applied the new scoring rules to your alliance’s game history. This recalculation ensures that past wins and losses are factored into your current rank more precisely. You may notice shifts in the leader board, but rest assured, these changes represent a more accurate picture of your alliance's performance.

[b]Decay System[/b]

To keep things competitive, alliances will now experience a gradual decay in their ELO scores. Alliances inactive for over 90 days will face even steeper declines. Stay active and engage in challenges to maintain your rank!

[b]Points System[/b]

The scoring system now takes into account the skill gap between winners and losers. No more easy wins for top alliances! If the difference between competing alliances is too large, no points will be awarded or lost. This adjustment levels the playing field and fosters fair competition.

[b]Ongoing Refinements[/b]

This system is a significant step forward, but it’s just the beginning. We’re actively monitoring its performance and refining it based on feedback from the community. Have ideas or suggestions? Share them with us in the feedback channels on Discord!

Thank you for your patience, engagement, and feedback throughout this journey. The future of alliances is brighter than ever, and we can’t wait to see how the new ELO system shapes the competitive scene.

notes.title: Elite Alliance Challenges
notes.notes:
[b]++++UPDATE++++[/b]

[b]Elite Challenges![/b]
Elite challenges are competitive matchups between alliances on maps where the use of gold is not allowed, ensuring a tournament level of fairness. This provides a more skill-driven and balanced environment for alliances eager to showcase their true competitive abilities.

[b]The time has come Alliance members! It's your time to shine![/b]
Starting in January, you'll have the chance to join Elite Challenge games and compete against other alliances to climb higher on the leader board. Prepare your alliance, gather your top players, and devise winning strategies, as you'll receive your first Elite ticket to challenge rival alliances in January.

[b]Elite Tickets[/b] 
In celebration of the return of Elite Challenges in January, the first tickets will be distributed to everyone, not just Security Council members. To qualify for these Elite tickets, you must be at least level 25 and have been active within the past 60 days. 
[i]Please note that for future Elite events, Security Council will be required to obtain the tickets.[/i]

[b]How do I use the Elite Tickets?[/b]
Tickets are used to participate in Elite challenge games after the opposing alliance leader accepts the challenge. Your ticket will only be consumed once you join the game and reach the Country selection screen. It's important to coordinate with your team and the opposing alliance leader, as we cannot oversee or intervene in any disputes or disagreements between players. To avoid issues, ensure clear communication with your alliance before using a ticket as tickets will not be refunded.

Keep in mind that Elite tickets are different from public event tickets. You will be able to hold both Elite tickets and Public tickets simultaneously, as they serve different purposes. Elite tickets are exclusively for elite alliance games, while Public tickets are used for public ticket events.

[b]That's the end of the briefing Commanders![/b]
Adapt to the changes, turn on “[b]Accept Challenges[/b]”, and in January the games begin!

notes.title: New ELO System
notes.notes:
[b]++++UPDATE++++[/b]

[b]Commanders![/b]
The new ELO system is just round the corner! The original ELO rankings didn't quite capture the dynamic alliance scene. After listening to our community a major overhaul has arrived to ensure a more competitive and representative system for alliances worldwide starting January. 

[b]Game History[/b]
The new ELO system will factor in your game history, recalculating your Alliance score by applying the updated point system to your past wins and losses. This adjustment aims to provide a more accurate reflection of your position on the leader board. While the revamped ELO system will deliver notable improvements to the alliance Elo calculation, you may notice changes in your leader board ranking due to the enhanced precision of the new calculations. The old Elo system hasn't always accurately reflected the alliance skillset due to its vulnerability to abuse, but we are now dedicated to making gradual improvements to address this issue.

[b]Decay System[/b]
To combat player inactivity, your Alliance ELO score will gradually decay over time. Staying active by playing challenges to maintain your rank is now crucial. Alliances inactive for over 90 days will see an even larger decline in their ELO score. This system rewards more for winning and penalizes less for defeat and was put in place to maintain a level playing field and reduce the ELO score discrepancy between Alliances.

[b]Points System[/b]
The scoring system now considers the score difference between winners and losers, preventing top alliances from preying on the inexperienced. This is a bully range that prevents victories from being too easy. If the score difference is beyond the bully range, none of the Alliances earn or lose points. The new system will be continuously monitored and refined to address and prevent any attempts by alliances to exploit it.

[b]Ongoing Refinements and Community Collaboration[/b]
We recognize that the system may not be flawless at launch, but it represents a significant improvement over the current one. We now have the flexibility to adjust the parameters more easily and can be fully transparent about how Elo is calculated.

During the holiday season, especially around Christmas when the team is on break, we'll still be active on Discord. We encourage all proactive and dedicated alliances to engage in the feedback channels to share ideas and discussions aimed at refining the calculations. Over time, this will help make the leader board increasingly representative and accurate.

[b]The future of CON Alliances is brighter than ever![/b]

In this new frozen world, the terrain has shifted, and not all soldiers or units are equipped for the harsh conditions. To address this challenge, we’re introducing a first for the game: A unit variant!

notes.title: THE NEW SCORING SYSTEM!
notes.notes:
[b]Attention Commanders![/b]

The upgrade was successful! We now have a new scoring system in place that promises to be more stable and accurate.

This system is responsible for tracking everything that happens during gameplay, such as units being eliminated or buildings being built, and converts those events into meaningful data like XP, ranks, and other player statistics. It often went down, causing players to temporarily see 0 XP and in some rare cases, XP earned from unit kills wasn't always accurate.

With the new system in place, players can expect more accurate XP calculations, ensuring that gameplay efforts are rewarded fairly. The system also offers improved stability, eliminating random drops in stats or disappearing XP, as it handles data more reliably with fewer disruptions. Additionally, updates will now roll out faster, making it easier to deploy changes and improvements to CoN.

This migration will introduce substantial improvements to the game, though you may notice some changes to your score due to more precise calculations in the new system. A small percentage of players might experience a slight decrease, but rest assured, these adjustments reflect the correct stats going forward. We appreciate your understanding and are confident that these improvements will benefit the game and your experience in the long run.

notes.title: Stims - New Tactical options, Realism, and Player Feedback
notes.notes:
[b]++++Comm-link++++[/b]

[b]Commanders, thank you for your feedback on our recent Stims announcement![/b]
We’re incredibly thankful for the community engagement and feedback given around the latest feature announcement: STIMS

With a lot of discussion happening in the community channels, we wanted to take the opportunity to speak more around the purpose, design decisions and future of stims! 


[b]Why Stims? Prioritizing Game Features[/b]
We’re always listening to your suggestions, and our feature roadmap is built on both community feedback and technical evaluations. We know features like Elite Games, sea mines, and more are highly requested, and they’re still part of our plans. 

In developing Stims, we executed on an opportunity to add a new dimension to gameplay, making it possible for players to strategize in more versatile ways that elevate the tactical aspect of Conflict of Nations.


[b]Realism[/b]
The foundation of CoN was developed with a commitment to a grounded, realistic strategy game. And we know how important this is to you. This approach garners the understandable reservation around the theme, surrounding the gameplay mechanic; Stims. 

Being a game grounded in reality, but pushing the limits of modern warfare, we want to balance gameplay with real-life inspiration. 

By design, we intentionally kept Stims open to interpretation while remaining rooted in modern conflict. Thematically, our approach is always centered around the core subject matter that is World War 3, which by nature (thankfully) is not a reality in itself. 

While "Stims" introduces a new layer of tactical depth, it is firmly based on modern advancements in real-world military science, which increasingly considers ways to improve soldier effectiveness through various enhancements. For us, Stims represent a grounded, if speculative, extension of real-world military innovation.

Our goal is to allow you to make more dynamic and impactful choices on the battlefield. Stims don’t change the fundamental realism of the game but rather open the door to more tactical decision-making within a realistic framework, providing a way to deploy your resources and tactical thinking in new and more flexible ways.


[b]Balancing Monetization[/b]
We understand the concern around monetization and want to assure you that we’re focused on balancing our economy fairly. While some elements of the game are monetized, we strive to provide a competitive, enjoyable experience for all players, regardless of their spending level. Stims will be accessible through in-game resources as well as direct purchases, allowing all players, including those who prefer not to spend, to benefit. 

The Pharmaceuticals required can be obtained by building a Secret Weapons Lab, creating an accessible, strategic layer. 

Additionally, we’re planning ongoing adjustments to ensure that Stims remain balanced, with every player able to use them as a strategic, short-term advantage rather than a constant overpowering force.

-
Your feedback remains crucial as we develop and evolve the game. Stims represent the first step in a series of upcoming features designed to bring greater depth and strategy, and we’re committed to fine-tuning and balancing them to meet your expectations.

Thank you for sharing your concerns and helping shape Conflict of Nations. We look forward to more discussions as we continue evolving the game you love.

Neutral units now remain safe from damage while within foreign territories and the command for air units to land on aircraft carriers has been removed. Intel accuracy has been refined to provide more reliable information on enemy forces, and event notifications now take you directly to the relevant location on the map.

We've also worked on visual and profile updates improvements. Vaults have been visually updated, and XP display errors in mobile user profiles have been corrected. Seasonal Special Forces now move at balanced speeds in enemy territories, and Max Rank accounts display ranks uniformly.

Beyond these fixes, we’ve polished the general menu interface for a cleaner, more responsive feel. Informative token pop-ups add clarity, and new web shop bundles with countdown timers help you seize timely offers.

notes.title: DORADO GAMES - 10th Year Anniversary!
notes.notes:
[b]Commanders![/b]

It's been a long wonderful journey filled with highs and lows, hard work and a great family. What once was a dream is now a reality that is growing by the day. Today, we’ve reached a significant milestone, bringing back countless memories that make it almost unbelievable to see how far we’ve come ,where we are now and where we are headed.

Dorado Games has come a long way in the past 10 years. What started from a vision has now become a talented team of over 40 members. Conflict of Nations wasn't the first game Dorado developed. A lot of hard work on previous projects led us to eventually create one of the top real-time war strategy games out there. While working for a game development company might sound fun(which it is), developing a game is far from simple. This isn't your typical 9-to-5 job where you can easily pick up where you left off the next day. Game development is a continuous effort that requires immense passion, drive, and creative qualities that are hard to find.

The Dorado team embodies this spirit. A passionate group brought together by a shared love for the game. Fast forward a few years, and we’ve grown into a thriving, active community with many developments on the horizon.

We’re not highlighting these milestones to brag, we see them as a stepping stone, as there’s still so much more to come for Conflict of Nations. We're just getting started! The real reason we’re saying this is to acknowledge that as much as the dorado team pushes the envelope, none of it would have been possible without you. A game is only as strong as its community, and we’re incredibly lucky to have a loyal player base that has helped us grow. This thank you goes out to everyone, not just beta testers, volunteers, or those who financially support the game. Every single player has made a difference, and we truly appreciate your support. You make all the countless hours worth it, and you make us proud!

We’re committed to taking Conflict of Nations even further, and we can’t wait to have you with us on this amazing journey!

To celebrate our 10th anniversary, we’re bringing back some classic maps into our rotation. Here’s what you can look forward to:

[b]Antarctica[/b] - 3 times daily
[b]Malta[/b] - 1 daily
[b]Squadron Cycle[/b] - 4 times daily

Throughout the development process, we went through several iterations and made numerous changes, especially in determining which countries would be AI-controlled and which would be playable. This collaborative approach allowed us to create a rich and immersive experience that reflects the unique dynamics of the region, making it a thrilling addition to our lineup!

We also had a blast interacting with our Discord community, where we welcomed player suggestions and made them happen, no matter how wild the ideas might be. It feels only fitting that this iteration of Squadron Cycle showcases the diverse range of seasonal units we’ve released over the years, bringing together the creativity of our team and the enthusiasm of our players into a dynamic and engaging scenario!

notes.title: The Making of - Antarctica Scenario
notes.notes:
[b]Antarctica Scenario[/b]

Antarctica was a project that began around 5 years ago, with three map designers contributing to its development. This project took particularly long to finish as we initially started working on it around the holidays in 2018. The intention was for it to be created for Alliance challenges, but the project was paused due to other priorities that came up and we ended up resuming progress on it a couple of years later.

This map was our first real dive into a part of the world not typically explored in our scenarios. Designed as a follow-up to Rising Tides, the concept centered around an Antarctic continent transformed into a habitable region, sparking a new wave of colonization by world powers. We used real-world maps as references while also envisioning how nations might carve up the continent in this future scenario.

notes.title: The Making of - Civil War Scenario
notes.notes:
[b]Civil War Scenario[/b]

Civil War emerged from our desire to create a scenario where North American states are thrown into a full-scale conflict. We started with the BG USA tutorial map but wanted to shift the focus entirely to North American states. To achieve this, we scaled the map up and reduced the presence of non-American nations as much as possible. However, due to geographical constraints, we included a few Canadian and Mexican nations, such as Ontario and Jalisco.

Our goal was to capture the chaos of a civil war, so we made every state playable, with all research unlocked from day one, creating a fast-paced and intense gameplay experience. To give players a chance to strategize before conflict erupted, we introduced a 24-hour peace timer. We also put extra focus on mountainous terrain by limiting connections, making these areas harder to traverse. This created natural defensive borders that offered players a stronger defensive approach.

We replaced the standard Motorized Infantry with Mechanized Infantry as starting units, giving the scenario a more modern feel and offering players stronger, more resilient units to defend their territories early in the game.

notes.title: The Making of - Nuclear Winter Scenario
notes.notes:
[b]Nuclear Winter Scenario[/b]

Nuclear Winter began with a simple “what if” question. One cold day, a few of us were outside chatting after hours when someone asked, “What if the world froze over? How devastating and life-changing would that be?” That little spark of conversation quickly turned into something bigger, and before we knew it, we were working on what would become one of the most beloved maps in Conflict of Nations!

Nuclear Winter isn't some scenario with a snowy backdrop and a couple of icy cosmetics, we wanted the ice to play a real role in how the game unfolds. That’s where icebergs and ice walls came in! These neutral, unconquerable obstacles appeared across land and sea, completely reshaping the map and challenging players to rethink their strategies with the introduction of new chokepoints and barriers.

Unlike most of our maps, where the tundra is typically confined to the far north, Nuclear Winter flipped the script covering the entire map in icy terrain. To mix things up even more, we added crater buildings to represent nuked cities, which helped even the playing field by weakening stronger nations from the start.
We also brought back some cool old features like Chosen and Domed Capitals. These gave the map a futuristic, post-apocalyptic vibe, paying homage to another fan favourite scenario: Rising Tides.

notes.title: The Making of - Sengoku Scenario
notes.notes:
[b]Sengoku Scenario[/b]

Sengoku was originally designed as a tutorial level specifically for our Japanese players, aiming to offer a localized experience, much like the success we had with BG USA and Flashpoint. We put a lot of effort into research and fine-tuning, to make this scenario as authentic and detailed as possible, especially when it came to representing Japan’s unique geography. We started with a 30-player count, but as we worked on it, we realized that there was potential for even more action, so we increased it to 60!

Sengoku ended up being the largest map we’d ever made in terms of geographic size, which really pushed the limits of our system. Thanks to all that extra space, we were able to include all 47 prefectures, even breaking Hokkaido into four distinct regions to add more depth. The whole process was a fun challenge, and it soon became clear that Sengoku was more than just a tutorial and it had the potential to be something much bigger.

So, in true Dorado style, we took things further! We reworked Sengoku into two highly successful event maps: Rising Sun and Nihon Nightmare. These maps took the foundation of Sengoku and expanded on it, creating dynamic new experiences that players have come to love!

notes.title: COMM-LINK - THE NEW SCORING SYSTEM
notes.notes:
[b]Attention Commanders![/b]

Our scoring and statistics system is undergoing a major upgrade! This system is responsible for tracking everything that happens during gameplay, such as units being eliminated or buildings being built, and converts those events into meaningful data like XP, ranks, and other player statistics.

Up to this point, we've been using an older version that was somewhat technologically outdated, making it tricky to maintain or improve resulting in some noticeable issues causing instability. It often went down, causing players to temporarily see 0 XP or empty stats on their profiles and in some rare cases, XP earned from unit kills wasn't always accurate.
We’re now happy to announce that we are migrating to a newer version of our Scoring System, a brand new version that promises to be more stable and accurate.

[b]With the new system soon in place, here’s what you can expect as a player:[/b]

[b]Improved XP accuracy:[/b] The XP you earn during the game will now be more precise, making sure that your gameplay efforts are rewarded fairly.

[b]Improved Stability:[/b] No more random drops in your stats or moments when your XP seems to disappear. The new system is built to handle data more reliably, meaning fewer disruptions.

[b]Faster Updates:[/b] It is now easier for us to deploy changes and improvements to the game, ensuring smoother updates.

While this migration will bring significant improvements to the game, you may notice some adjustments to your score, as the new system will provide more accurate calculations. While this could result in a slight reduction for a small percentage of players, please know that these updates are reflective of the correct stats moving forward. We appreciate your understanding and are confident that these improvements will benefit the game and your experience in the long run.

We appreciate your patience and support during this migration. 
[b]See you on the Battlefield![/b]

notes.title: DRONE OPERATOR - DEVLOG
notes.notes:
[b]Introducing the Drone Operator – A New Era of Warfare[/b]

[b]Attention Commanders![/b]
In this latest season of Conflict of Nations, we’re excited to unveil a brand-new unit that reflects both modern warfare and the evolving nature of our game: the Drone Operator. As battlefields change, so must your strategy. This unit is equipped with three distinct drone types that will fundamentally alter how you approach the fight against the undead and the living. Here’s a breakdown of these new tools at your disposal and a glimpse behind the scenes into why we felt drones were a crucial addition to the game.

[b]Why Drones?[/b]
When we first started designing “Conflict of Nations”, our focus was firmly on the Cold War era, but as the game has evolved and the world of war has changed, so has our vision. Over the past few years, drones have become a dominant force in modern warfare as they are defining the battlefields of today.

Incorporating drones into CoN was a natural evolution. By adding them, we’re able to expand the air vs. anti-air mechanics. This gives players more tactical options. The Drone Operator and its three drones represent this shift. We wanted to give you a taste of what these advanced tools could do in real-life scenarios, while also providing a fresh layer of strategy for CoN. The Recon, Explosive, and Sabotage drones offer a variety of tactical possibilities, from gathering intelligence to delivering devastating strikes on key enemy positions.

At its core, the drone operator showcases the direction we see the game heading: embracing modern warfare innovations while offering players new ways to outsmart their opponents.
 
[b]The Drones:[/b] 
This season, we’re handing you the reins to a drone squad equipped with highly specialized units, each serving a vital role on the battlefield.

[b]Recon Drone[/b]
Every successful battle begins with intelligence, and the Recon Drone is your key to gathering it. While unarmed, its real power lies in its ability to scout out zombie infestations across provinces. Knowledge is power – spotting potential threats early allows you to strategize more effectively, avoid unnecessary risks, and maximize your troops’ chances of survival.

[b]Explosive Drone[/b]
Sometimes, the best way forward is to clear the path, literally. The Explosive Drone is a one-way ticket for dealing massive damage to zombie hordes. Its sacrificial nature makes it an invaluable tool for weakening groups of zombies, setting the stage for your soldiers to swoop in and clean up the remaining resistance. Used strategically, it’s a powerful way to soften up enemy forces before committing ground troops.

[b]Sabotage Drone[/b]
Hives pose a serious threat to your cities, capable of expanding the zombie infestation if left unchecked. Enter the Sabotage Drone. This anti-structure drone is designed to directly target and damage these organic formations, buying you time and space to reclaim infected regions. It’s a precision strike tool for turning the tide when faced with a spreading infestation.

[b]In this season, the sky is no longer the limit, it's your new battleground.[/b]

In this dark new season, the struggle for survival intensifies as a deadly virus has turned the dead into relentless hordes. [b]Introducing the new Drone Operator.[/b]

This unit's main function is to utilize drones as versatile tools, each with unique capabilities tailored for different strategic roles. The good news is that in “[b]Z Resurgence[/b]” everyone starts off with a drone operator!

[b]The Drones![/b]
This season introduces three powerful drone types, each with unique capabilities to help you on the battlefield.
[list][*][b]Reco Drone[/b]
An essential reconnaissance tool, the Reco Drone is unarmed but invaluable. It allows you to spot zombie infestations in provinces, enabling you to plan your assaults effectively and avoid unnecessary risks.

[/*][*][b]Explosive Drone[/b]
Sacrificing itself for the greater good, the Explosive Drone is designed to deal severe damage to zombie hordes, weakening them before your soldiers move in for the final assault. Use these drones strategically to clear the path for your troops.

[/*][*][b]Sabotage Drones[/b]
A strategic anti-structure drone designed to inflict damage on the hives. Hives are organic formations capable of causing devastating damage if not addressed promptly. It is crucial to deal with infected cities and regions immediately, as neglect will lead to a large spread infestation.[/*][/list]

[b]Z Resurgence[/b]
This season's map, Z Resurgence, plunges you into a 100-player, zombie-infested world where your survival instincts will be pushed to the limit. As you navigate this treacherous landscape, you'll face the daunting challenge of handling relentless zombie hives and hordes while simultaneously defending against neighboring countries competing for control. How will you balance the threats from the undead and rival nations in this high-stakes battle for survival?

[b]Vaults and Havens[/b]
In Z Resurgence, capturing Vaults and Havens will significantly strengthen your army. Not only will you earn Victory Points when in control of these points of interest, but these structures will also serve as crucial sources for generating Manpower as manpower production has shifted from provinces to Vaults and Havens in Z Resurgence.

Players will start with slightly reduced manpower production but will have two vaults within its borders. Vaults, which are abundant, are crucial for sustaining your forces, while Havens being so rare and located in zombie-controlled territories, offer much higher manpower boosts.

[b]Zombie Hives and Territories[/b] 
Certain areas are under zombie control from the start, making their reconquest a top priority.
You’ll begin with a [b]Drone Operator[/b] in your capital, along with an [b]Air Superiority Fighter[/b] and 2 [b]Motorized Infantry[/b] units.
Zombie-infested cities and hives pose significant threats, making recon and strategic assaults vital. This map will push your strategic thinking to its limits as reclaiming your homeland has never been harder

[b]Unit Combos[/b]
When dealing with zombie threats, make sure to prioritize deploying the Elite Attack Aircraft, as it's highly effective at wiping out enemies in its path. Focus on achieving air superiority to better protect your ground forces and assist drone operators with reconnaissance missions. Coordinate with frontline units to use the aircraft as the initial strike force.

Keep in mind that while these aircraft are expensive to deploy and maintain, they offer a powerful advantage by attacking zombie hordes from above, taking full advantage of the fact that zombies can't defend against aerial assaults. Pairing these airstrikes with drone attacks will give you the critical edge needed to combat the infection effectively.

[b]Good luck, Commanders.[/b] 
The future of humanity is in your hands!

notes.title: The Art of Alliance War: Unveiling a New Era of ELO Rankings!

notes.title: DEV LOG #27: CoNquering Mobile Woes
notes.notes:
[b]CoNquering Mobile Woes: Our Devs Step into the Light to Fix Performance Issues![/b]

 

Sometimes it’s good to take a step back and reflect on progress. This year has proven to be a period of steady growth for Conflict of Nations. We have a lot of different projects in the pipeline, intended to continue improving gameplay experience, introduce new features and generally provide an even better overall experience to all our players.

 

However, we particularly love our dedicated team of developers. So we decided to usher them out of their dark dungeons, away from the fizzling energy drinks and local Twistee snack, and into the bright world of performance fixes. Much to their chagrin, they spent copious amounts of time trying to break the app and trying to understand why some things work as intended, while others frequently decide to call it quits at the worst of times. 

 

“What’s the point of all this”, you’re probably wondering. Well let me paint you a picture. For the past years, we’ve been wrestling (rasslin) with a medley of issues across diverse mobile devices. Our app, despite its quirks, occasionally chose to play hide-and-seek, depriving some players of the full joy of Conflict of Nations. The desktop experience is stellar, no doubt, but who can resist the thrill of triggering a nuclear detonation from your pocket while brunching with friends or grocery shopping? Hence, refining the app is an important tick on our daily to-do list.

 

And so we go back to our stressed out devs looking through the code and through our game, and boy did we find some real performance guzzlers.. As with any technology we’re still not sure why certain things happen, and that will forever remain a fact we must accept in our hearts. Nevertheless, we decided to dedicate a considerable amount of time to making fixes for our mobile app. 

 

For those of you on Discord, you might recall us asking for feedback about the app itself, and any performance issues you’ve encountered. That was a veritable goldmine of information and we are extremely grateful for the points which were made over there!

 

This won’t be a one-time round of fixes for sure and we don’t expect everything to work perfectly once we release. However, we do hope that it makes a difference for our players and that the experience on the app is much more enjoyable as a result.

 

In fact, some time ago, we discussed the fabled and mysterious Update Intake, which was preparing a lot of opportunities for us to delve into more dedicated performance fixes and paving the way for new features in the future. What is Update Intake you might ask? [strike]We have absolutely no idea[/strike] It is a massive technical undertaking where we are updating the original code that provides for the foundation of Conflict of Nations in order to modernize it. As Yak so rightly put it back in a previous Dev Log about Update Intake, it’s like taking an old car engine and improving it with the latest engineering developments. The point of all this? It allows us more flexibility with our code to allow new features to be implemented and added, which also means we can be more creative with future features! 

 

This is merely the starting line and, while we don't promise an instant utopia post-release, we're committed to significantly enhancing your gaming experience. Our aspiration? To make the app journey more seamless, enjoyable, and memorable for all our players.

 

As we prepare to set sail on this exciting journey, we invite you to join us in anticipating an exhilarating future. Stay tuned and keep your eyes on the horizon, the best is yet to come!

After that massive update intake, which you can learn more about in Dev Log #24, we are excited to confirm that elite frigates and aircraft carriers can now be stacked like other units! This comes together with a more general range of fixes for carrier issues that have been experienced over the past months!

But that’s not all, our developers have been hard at work to introduce some changes to the functionality of air units. Whenever a stack of air units loses its origin airfield, whether this is a normal airport or a carrier, planes will instead look for the closest airport depending on the range of the different units types in that stack. This will either be based on the ferry range of the unit if it is idle, or the attack range in case the unit is in action during the time the airbase is destroyed. If you are in a coalition or have right of way with another country, then allied airports will also be considered for the relocation of the air units. Depending on the different types of air units in a single stack, the stack will divide into multiple different stacks. For example a stack of helicopters and bombers will split into a stack of helicopters and a separate stack for bombers. If there are no available places in range for planes to land safely, they will instead crash immediately. This also means that air units will not convert to a transport truck anymore under any circumstances.

notes.title: DEV LOG #24 Mommy, what's a Update Intake?
notes.notes:
We’re back!

 

Our first update was released some days ago! While it may not look like much on the surface, bellowing beneath the game visuals is a new modular package of goodness infused into the long running Supremacy engine which we have built the CoN foundations upon.

 

Internally this package is colloquially known as 'Update intake'.

 

To understand this, we need to take a trip down Stillfront-lane. I promise we’ll take the express lane.

 
[h3][b]It was the best of times, it was the worst of times[/b][/h3]
 

When Bytro built the Supremacy engine way back when (most of us still had hair), they expanded the engine to accommodate the games they developed. Supremacy, Call of War, Thirty Kingdoms, New World Empires, and later Iron Order.

 
[h3][b]A whole new world[/b][/h3]
 

Between New World Empires and Thirty Kingdoms, Dorado Games entered the scene tasked with a mission; [strike]We kill th[/strike] Use the Supremacy Engine and take it on for the next project. To get our blades sharpened, we used the ongoing Thirty Kingdoms game taking it apart and putting it back while applying our company touch. This, of course, meant getting [i]very[/i] familiar with the Supremacy engine, along with all its quirks and supremacy.

 

Blitzkrieg to end 2016, after a very intense number of seasons, Dorado packaged and released Conflict of Nations into the stratosphere (take [i]that[/i] Tesla) through an open public Beta. During this time and to this day, Bytro and Dorado work on separate codebases but still maintain very close contact including (but not limited to) cross-company support across departments.

 
[h3][b][strike]1984[/strike] 2023[/b][/h3]
 

Fastforward again some years, (some? It’s been almost 6 years - oof I’m getting old)

 

My existential crisis aside, the two companies [strike]lived happily ever after[/strike] diligently, and with great fervour worked on their games in an unrelenting manner with the aim of utmost dedication. (Seriously, I’ve been in those meetings.)

 

Over time our codebases grew very differently from one another. Now, for the technically inclined of you, this probably rings some alarm bells. But for sake of the normal folk, this means that one company had a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, while another had a pineapple pizza (I’ll let you be the judge of who has what). The problem here is; we somehow had to merge the two dishes [i]while making it work[/i].

 

And here we are! What? I said we’ll take the express lane, I only kind of lied.

 
[h3][b]What were you talking about again? I’m hungry now.[/b][/h3]
 

Yes! Update intake. Thanks for reminding me. For the better part of last year one of our developers had the monumental task of merging the two savoury dishes that have no complimentary qualities. The peanut butter and sandwich is the base, as is the pizza with sauce and mozzarella. The Jelly and Pineapple? Well, you see the problem here.

 

More technically speaking, update intake adds in some modernised code on the underlying engine of our game. Another way of thinking about it is in this way: We took the engine of a car from years ago, and infused the engineering of progress made over the past years.

 

You will [b]not[/b] see visual changes, and may not perceive any changes at all, but the intake allows us greater flexibility in improving the underlying code. Oh! Also, it fixes a fair bit of bugs and optimisation issues which were causing headaches. It’s one of those black magic things which touches on so many areas that it isn’t so clear cut as to what is fixed and improved.

 
[h3][b]Here Be Dragons[/b][/h3]
 

We spent quite some weeks and months making preparations for Update intake, in past week having the beta testers mercilessly break our beta environment (with consent). But, alas, such is the nature of development, we cannot know the full effects until live release. Thankfully, with 2 days since release we haven’t seen very many bugs, actually, it went much better than expected!

 

The team scrambled together 3 Hotfixes since then, and things are looking delicious! We aren’t out of the kitchen yet, tracking down pesky bugs as they make themselves known. Given sensitivity of the situation we’ve been very quick to identify and fix said bugs. Even [i]they [/i]couldn’t resist the allure of PBJ pineapple pizza.

 

Believe it or not, yes we made PBJ & Pineapple pizza work. If you ask how? Honestly, the dedication of everyone at Dorado. We’re monitoring very closely but internally this is considered a success all things considered.

 
[h3][b]It’s been 87 years[/b][/h3]
 

I think that concludes this lengthy [strike]rant[/strike] post for devlog 23. As it stands, we’re finalising the roadmap for 2023 which I will gladly share with you once we have. We have some other interesting things in the short term pipeline which I’ll be showing [i]soon[/i].

 

Also, we’re looking for [i]another [/i]sacrificial dev for the [i]next[/i] update intake. Now excuse me while I prepare lunch.

 

- Yak

notes.title: Season 9 is Live!
notes.notes:
+++++ SEASON 9 IS LIVE ++++
Featuring: Elite Frigate

The Time has come,
The long-awaited
The one and only,
Is it a jet-ski, is it a whale?
It’s the Elite Frigate!

We have been teasing and discussing the Elite Frigate for some time now! We have noted the challenges involved in making this new unit a reality, but now the time has come and we are ready to go with Season 9!

The Elite Frigate is a support surface vassal capable of servicing helicopters to further improve your Navy's combat operations. As a ship - whilst it can take a beating, it is not designed for direct combat and should ideally be kept out of harm’s way, and not used to directly engage hostile ships.

The unit starts off as a capable Anti-Sub deterrent, and provides the fleet with an early warning detection against hostile helicopters. The unit can carry two Helicopters from the get-go, allowing you to further enhance its combat ability against Submarines, provide it with better reconnaissance capabilities, or give it the ability to provide helicopter air-support to ground operations.

Once you begin to upgrade the unit, it really starts to shine. 

Tier 2
At tier two, it can carry an additional Helicopter, bringing it up to 3. The unit gains the ability to launch Cruise Missiles, giving it further ability to neutralize distant targets, be they sea or land. The ship gains the ability to launch Loitering Munitions, allowing you to either cover a retreat, or cover an area to intercept hostile units.

Tier 3
At Tier 3 - The ship gains more cruise missile capabilities. Giving it a strong ability to serve as a primary cruise missile launch platform. On-top of that, the ship gains strong anti-missile defence capabilities, improving your fleet's survivability. At this tier - the unit has a low-signature, allowing it to sneak past most radar systems available - save for the very best and finely tuned radar systems.

Note: The new unit will only be available in NEW games which are spawned after release.


As many players who have been with us in previous Seasons are aware, we also offer a previous Seasonal Unit to give players a chance to experience those units again. This time around, we have 2 previous seasonal units on offer. 

Elite Loitering Munitions and the Main Battle Tank are both making a comeback only for a Limited time!

Those of you who haven’t had a chance to permanently unlock these units before can now have another crack at it during Season 9! Security Council members need 500 Points in this Season for permanent unlock of the Loitering Munitions, and 2,500 points for the Main Battle Tank..

In case this is your first Season, here’s a rundown how Seasons work:
Earn Season Points by killing units in any of your games - they all count!
Try out the unique Seasonal Units, available to everyone! (NOTE: Only available for new games starting now)
The Season Units can be researched from a new tab in the Research Panel. Any Elite units you have already unlocked from previous seasons are fully able to be mobilized in any game of your choice!

In order to permanently unlock the Seasonal Unit and use it after the Season ends you must earn at least 1,500 Seasonal Points for the Elite Frigate, and also have a valid Security Council Pass.

You will find all the details [url=https://bit.ly/3G2eafn]here[/url].

notes.title: DEV LOG #023
notes.notes:
+++++SEASON 9 UNIT - ELITE FRIGATE+++++

EU: Bromo-Class, Western: Constellation-Class, Eastern: Admiral-Gorshkov-Class

Anyone with us for a long time will have heard the stories about how we never could offer variations on carriers or units such as Amphibious Assault Ships or the like. This is now changing: due to the ongoing refactoring of the relevant code and the time we are needing finalizing the programming, we are currently working on also finalizing the design side of the new unit.

For the first time we are actually touching the “Carrier Code” of the game, allowing a unit besides the aircraft carrier to serve as a mobile launching platform for air units - in this case: helicopters.

Our unit of choice at the time of writing, for the upcoming Season is an ELITE FRIGATE with the following design principles which need to be adhered to:
1. The unit will come in three visual models as per the artworks
2. All three units will be interchangeable in stats, so no dedicated faction/doctrine
3. The tech tree must differentiate three research levels per Elite Frigate

With regards to the features it will have, it will offer the ability to host helicopter(s) onboard, at one stage of the research tree. A list of features that will also be included, derived from other ships are:

Research Cost/Time, 

Mobilization Cost/Time, 

Day Available, 

Hit Points, 

Speed, 

Attack/Defence vs XYZ, 

Sight/Radar/Sonar Ranges, 

Helicopter Slots, 

Cruise Missile Slots, 

Ability to deploy Loitering Munitions, 

Stealth/Stealth Detection, 

AA Range/Envelope, … to name the most obvious. 

While we do not envisage any issues going forward, the unit is obviously subject to change. Nevertheless, we are midway through development. We look forward to receiving any feedback you might like to pass on to us as we now enter the final stages of the run up to Season 9!

And now fair winds and following seas while designing this new vessel.

notes.title: DEV LOG 22
notes.notes:
+ + + + DEV LOG: 22 + + + + 

Commanders!

It's your local friendly Community lead here - Yak. When I'm nowhere to be found on our platforms, it's safe to say we're all giving headaches to the developers and producers! (They are happy to oblige) Why you might ask? Well! The designers are cooking up quite some spicy dishes, with an entree of assorted (and exquisite) taste breakers; I'm excited to disclose what's on the menu for the coming months from the rag tag bunch over at Dorado. Without further ado, let's get cracking. 
[list][*]Amphibious Fighting Vehicle:[list][*]After looking at the stats behind Amphibious Fighting Vehicle, the general consensus was that they are relatively underused, but not exceptionally so. We suspect that the research tree path might be an influence here, and for a first iteration we we are updating the Amphibious Fighting Vehicle to be separated from the Armored Fighting Vehicle research path, along with all the respective upgrades irrespective of each other. This is coming [u]very soon.[/u][/*][/list][/*][*]Air-Assault can use Carriers:[list][*]In real world scenarios, carriers are used to launch air-assault operations regularly. A function absent from the current implementation of CoN, adding this change is an interesting proposition given that Air Assault can definitely benefit from it along with Naval skirmishes. 

Thus, changes to Air-assault units are coming! We will soon allow Air-Assault able units to use carriers as launch points, extending the range they can use to Air-assault. We anticipate this to be available [u]before [/u]the release of Season 9.[/*][/list][/*][*]Helicopter Carrier:[list][*]The aircraft carrier is pretty expensive, and serves a pretty important role. We want to emphasize that. As a naval player, this is your capital ship. However, there's some aspects of the aircraft carrier which the Heli Carrier should be able to handle in the early game, or at least serve as a way for naval players to put pressure on their foes beyond their coastal cities. Moreover, this helps make helicopters more attractive as an option. 

With the current implementation of Carriers, it is a more attractive choice to focus on aircraft rather than helicopters (at least in some instances). In light of this, we are working on a new unit that will act as a cheaper-costing variant of the Aircraft Carrier. The Helicopter Carrier is able to carry helicopters and act as an HQ (base of operations) for the helicopters, like any other airport would. This unit will not be a seasonal unit. This update is also expected sometime after Season 9.[/*][/list][/*][*]Ship carry-capacity[list][*]Carry-capacity is something that we haven't really touched in CON previously. Transport ships fill that role. But units like the Heli Carrier and Aircraft Carrier regularly carry compliments of troops to engage in ground operations. This is the most experimental feature/idea until now, and as it stands we are exploring options and brainstorming ideas on expanding gameplay in this domain. We don't have a lot of specifics here as the feature is in it's infancy production-wise. The general idea is to give ships the ability to utilize carry-capacity for units. This will allow them to transport units faster than if they were transport ships. Eventually, it will allow units like the Airborne infantry to 'ferry' to the aircraft carrier. This will require a fair bit of development, definitely will be after Season 9.[/*][/list][/*][/list]
--

In other news, just in case you missed our last Dev log, we officially [url=https://forum.conflictnations.com/index.php?thread/11620-developer-diary-21-interface-fusion-q4/]announced[/url] our plans to give a much needed facelift to the Desktop client of the game, updating the user interface and graphics style. You can see previews and ask questions [url=https://forum.conflictnations.com/index.php?thread/11613-unified-client-preview-questions-and-answers/]here[/url].

Since our last log, players have come forward with some questions which I am going to be sharing here as well for everyone.

Player question: Does this mean that the Desktop client ([url=http://conflictnations.com/]conflictnations.com[/url]) will become like the Mobile (Android/iPhone) client?
Answer: Not exactly, no. We will be updating the [b]graphics [/b](Sea, provinces, user interface art style) to look much closer to mobile. But, we will be doing more work to make sure that user interface and experience is [b]adapted and reworked[/b] to keep desktop in mind. This means widgets such as the command dial, will not be on the new client.

Player question: Are the User Interface differences between Desktop and Mobile going to preserve the best elements of both?
Answer: That is the best case scenario, yes. Truthfully though, [b]on launch[/b] there won't be all the features/implementations done yet. It will be a tiered approach, of course, keeping in mind community/player feedback. As I said in my original post. [b]Players, have the option to opt out of the new client [/b]for months (if not year) after Beta launch, so you will be in a position to voice your feedback while being relatively unaffected using the 'classic' client.

Player question: Do our accounts reset to level 1?
Answer: No. Your account will remain untouched and fully functional without losing anything.

Player question: Will this change game mechanics?
Answer: No. The base game remains exactly the same, unless an update states otherwise to improve the game.

 

And with that, this log is at an end. Until the next one! GLHF!

notes.title: Join the CON League!
notes.notes:
+ + + + ALLIANCE LEAGUE + + + +

In case you've been living under a Carrier, today we've been dedicating the day to Discord, with a flood of Community Managers taking the front to give you maps, and entertainment. Antarctica and Able Archer will be open for the Discord-republic [u]for a limited time[/u]. The keen eyed of you also should have seen that we officially announced collaboration with the Alliance League. Today, I am also happy to further announce details of the League - without further ado:

DATE: 

The CON League has a tentative start date for November 2022 for the upcoming Season.

IS MY ALLIANCE READY?

The CON League tries to include all Alliances possible in its organized events. However, proper competition requires Alliances to have certain prerequisites to join in the Seasonal competition. These include:
[olist][*]A minimum of 7 players within the Alliance (less than 7 is eligible to join the Beginner's Circuit, but not the Seasonal competition)[/*][*]Have played Alliance Matches within the last 6 months (in order to determine if they understand how Alliance Matches work)[/*][*]Have the player capacity to participate in Elite Matches (enough players with the rank 25+)[/*][/olist]

HOW TO APPLY:

The CON League is open for all Alliances to apply. They only need to fill out a Dyno Form which submits their application directly to the League server to be reviewed. Here is a copy of the Form: [url=https://dyno.gg/form/e9d3358f]https://dyno.gg/form/e9d3358f[/url]. Alliances can also find the League directly in the League server, if they are already on the server.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

Alliances participating in the CoN League receive points when they defeat another alliance, allowing them to move up in the rankings of their particular division. The more you win, the more points you will score as the season goes on.At the end of the Season, the top two Alliances move up to the next Division, while the bottom two Alliances drop down to a lower Division. This system is in effect in order to naturally move Alliances based on their skill, performance and ability.

PRIZES

Prizes for the CON League is thanks to our wonderful association and partnership with the parent company Dorado. The prize for the top Alliances in the Seasonal competition includes the choice of whatever Season badge that they desire. Possible future prizes are in discussion.

 MISC.

Alliances participating within the CON League have the ability to negotiate with their opponent about map type and other rules in a mutually agree ruleset. The most standard map utilized within the League is the MED map, although all other map types are available for use.

The League hosts occasional tournaments, Battle Royales, and roleplaying games. The League is officially open for outside organizations/individuals, regardless of membership status within the League, to partner with the League to host their own tournament, BR, or RP. Details of the Tourney/BR/RP would be regulated by League rules/regulations, and would be monitored for quality assurance. This allows those who have trouble running their own special events have an outlet, and it allows the League to further nurture the Community and expand its outreach.

notes.title: Developer Diary 21: INTERFACE FUSION Q4
notes.notes:
GREETINGS FELLOW CONMANDERS! Yak here! 
(my colleagues hate when I do that, maybe it's because they aren't morning people? or maybe exclaiming it at 160 decibels isn't to their tastes, go figure)

I come bearing news! Much of it actually. So I hope you have some [u]hours[/u] time set aside for the fun process that is reading our dev log! This one is a lengthy one, we've been very busy on a number of fronts and I want to make sure that I can contain as many responses to common player sentiments as possible.
[h2][u][b]State of the team[/b][/u][/h2]
For a while now we've been seeing a very nice uptick in players adopting CoN, lending to an increase in demand which, naturally, means our technical systems have more people to keep up with. There have been many optimizations in past months, and there are more to come. More on that in this post below.

Naturally this meant Dorado needed to bolster forces through employment of developers, and managers from all walks of life, to add to our repertoire of special forces-like staff. In due time I would like to host Q&A/AMA sessions to introduce the new(and old) blood behind Dorado.
[h2][u][b]Design changes and balance[/b][/u][/h2]
Feedback on the Season 8 unit has been plentiful, and discussions hot to the touch. As I type this - the designated game designer (Codename Lunar on our Discord) is revisiting the balance for the Elite Attack Aircraft, bearing in mind the discussions held on our [url=https://forum.conflictnations.com/index.php?thread/11432-opinions-on-the-season-8-unit-elite-attack-aircraft/]forum[/url] and the data we have available.

As it stands our analysis indicates that; Air Superiority Fighters are now the most built aircraft (not by a lot) - which is good to see as it is part of our intention with the unit feature of Season 8, to promote viability of the Superiority Fighter. Speaking of Strike Fighters, the base unit is built more than its Elite counterpart, the Attack Aircraft. (This being said, the Elite Attack Aircraft has a higher total construction count in 4x maps). Looking at the data holistically, there seems to be a nice spread between Air Superiority fighters, Strike Fighters, and Elite Attack Aircraft, indicating to us that a conservative balance is the right way to go.

We are also looking into tweaking the Elite Helicopter unit, but this is still early, right now the main priority is Elite Attack Air.
[h2][u][b]Brand new desktop client[/b][/u][/h2]
I anticipate this project will worry some of our veterans, but I want to address any concerns here as clearly as possible to avoid any misunderstandings.
Firstly I want to explain; what is the new Desktop client going to be?

For a bit of context, as it stands, we are having to maintain and update two projects independent of one another: Desktop(Web i.e. [url=http://conflictnations.com/]conflictnations.com[/url]) as it is right now in its current state, and the Mobile Application.
[h3][b][u]What does this mean?[/u]
[/b][/h3]
Many issues and updates need to be developed for each platform, costing us at least twice the time and resources it would otherwise.
[h3][u][b]Why is this bad?[/b][/u][/h3]
Naturally it is very inefficient use of our time, especially when you consider that bugs or problems can be introduced on platforms independent of each other, meaning we also need to fix said issues twice at times.
This is also stopping us from adopting new features and implementing new systems since we know that it will need to be ported to mobile and vice versa. Once the process is done we will be on a much more efficient schedule of infusing brand new content and changes on a regular basis.
[h3][u][b]What can be done?[/b][/u][/h3]
To fix this, we are working behind the scenes to merge the two platforms, Mobile and Desktop. This does not mean that a simple port to Desktop will be made. We are working on entirely overhauling the User Interface, and User Experience, especially tailored to Desktop and its use case.
There are also a wealth of changes which will come along, modernizing the look and feel of CoN more inline with 2022 standards. Graphics will also be getting a major overhaul similar in similar fashion to Mobile in it's current state. With this being said, Mobile will not see any changes. The unification will largely leave Mobile audiences unaffected with the exception of getting the benefits from the better efficient developer team working behind the game!
[h3][u][b]But I don't want that![/b][/u][/h3]
We understand that people are afraid of such a big change. We are working very closely with the community to address any issues for the Beta launch, to ensure that the new transition is seamless and pleases our core playerbase, which is found on Desktop(Web).
I want to make it absolutely clear, we are not simply porting Mobile to Desktop(Web). Unit control, interface popups, dialogue options etc. will all be revised from the ground up to cater to the platform and player needs.
[h3][u][b]But I still don't want that[/b][/u][/h3]
Worry not! We are going to give all players the option to keep using the old client for a time period. Be informed though, that we will not be updating the old client with brand new interface features and quality of life changes, save for some critical bug fixes.
[h3][u][b]When?[/b][/u][/h3]
Internally the title for this project is Unified client. The Beta release is slated for release on the fourth quarter of 2022. As I mentioned above, if you do not find the initial release to your liking you will be given the option to revert to the old client, unaffected by the new changes.
[h3][u][b]I'm curious now[/b][/u][/h3]
As of writing this, the most fleshed out portion of our overhaul has been done on the main menus. You can find early mockup previews for the first time ever! -[url=https://forum.conflictnations.com/index.php?thread/11613-unified-client-questions-and-answers/]here[/url]. It is crucial I mention that this is not final at all and everything you see is subject to change.
I understand there will be plenty of questions, post any and all questions you have [url=https://forum.conflictnations.com/index.php?thread/11613-unified-client-questions-and-answers/]here [/url]so that we can address them.
[h2][u][b]In other news[/b][/u][/h2]
That's not all! We have a lot ongoing tasks and projects.
[h3][u][b]Merch Shop[/b][/u][/h3]
You read that right! We are working on finally getting an official Conflict of Nations merch store up and running. The good news? It will be live very soon. In a matter of weeks if all goes according to plan. Our resident artists worked hard on pitching exclusive designs you're sure to love. As the times roll on, we will be updating the availability of designs and products, so make sure to be quick to buy anything you like as items are likely to be there for a limited time only.
[h3][u][b]Discord 40,000 Members[/b][/u][/h3]
That's right! Our [url=http://discord.gg/con]official Discord[/url] server reached 40k members! A number many of us are very fond of at the office, being Warhammer geeks.
To commemorate this special milestone - we have a very special day planned. Keep your eyes peeled for all the details next week.
Also, in case you've been living under an Abrams, we host weekly events on our Discord server and Twitter!
[h3][u][b]Update intake[/b][/u][/h3]
We are doing a lot of work on the player-facing portions of the game, like UI/UX, client etc. This is not to say we are neglecting the underlying foundations entirely. Far from it. We are working extensively on refactoring and adopting bug fixes on our game engine. This will involve optimizations, with benefits having an effect on performance and loading times, as well as much needed bug fixes.
[h3][u][b]Dynamic Victory points[/b][/u][/h3]
We are working on the way victory points are updated, right now they update at the end of ingame day. This will change to update dynamically as soon as a change is required. This is WIP.

notes.title: PSA: Upgrading The Services
notes.notes:
Dear Commanders,
 

As of late we've seen an unprecedented number of players take up Conflict of Nations, and other games belonging to our sister company, Bytro.
 

While this is indeed a very welcome addition, we very quickly needed to shift our day to day operations to cater to the sheer volume of demand. From early on in March we have had the Developers monitor the situation day and night, and will continue to do so even after we have the developments outlined below. Particularly, what is affecting the game so much is the concurrent requests and demands taking place at peak hours of activity. We have been scaling the backend services as much as possible, but there are roadblocks which we could not have planned for. All this being said we are taking this in strides and using it as an opportunity to do right by the players and community. We are overhauling much of the underlying functionality which will provide better service all-round.
 

As it stands, we have a number of high priority changes which will make their way into the game in the coming weeks:[list][*]Game creation: This system is responsible for spawning games and handling the funneling process of new players into their tutorial games. We are seeing this system cause a heavy strain with the scale of players. This task is marked as critical in terms of priority and planned for a complete overhaul.[/*][*]Game updates: Ingame commands and game status need to be polled and updated on a regular basis. We are seeing high processing costs here which can be cut without player interference. This is a high priority task which is planned for a rework for better efficiency.[/*][*]Multithreading: In layman terms - currently our server infrastructure and game are not optimized to utilize concurrent player requests/commands in a particularly efficient manner. We are revisiting the approach taken and marked this as a high priority task for rework to better cater to parallel user requests.[/*][*]Call prioritizations: In cases where concurrent player requests come through as noted above, we are working further to make sure that these player requests are prioritized in order of importance. This is a high priority task.[/*][*]Push Notifications, Research: With the amount of strain on our servers and web calls, a traffic jam occurs. A single action such as Push Notifications to your phone will create an incredible traffic jam on the services. For the time being we have disabled or tweaked some of the functionality like Push Notifications, but other game functionalities such as the Research tree criteria and other linked items cannot be disabled. We have a number of tweaks and changes planned for this High priority task to cater for ever growing game and activity.[/*][/list]
 
Dorado are working closely with Bytro to get these updates out to you as soon as possible. Right now we have an estimated date of 3 - 4 weeks until all the above can be injected into the game, [b]but we will be adding the above changes to the game as soon as they are individually available[/b] - so improvements will take place gradually over these weeks, starting [b]from tomorrow[/b].
 

In any case we will keep the community informed on any intel as soon as we receive it. We wholeheartedly apologize for the subpar performance of the game in the recent days. Believe us when we take no joy in seeing players encounter roadblocks to playing the game they've come to know and love. Our promise is to improve it as soon as possible and is our absolute, utmost priority right now above all.

notes.title: NEW MAP: WESTERN THEATER
notes.notes:
+ + + + UPDATE + + + +

Commanders - we’re happy to announce a brand new map ready for strategic conquest starting NOW.

NEW Map: Western Theater 

In the aftermath of Battlegrounds USA - the once United States of America are now fractured, and turmoil envelops the continent in civil war. As for the Eastern front, a new revolution is threatening the powers that be. Europe takes center stage in all this, as nations scramble to fill the lingering power vacuum. 

Deriving many of the good qualities from Battleground USA and Flashpoint maps - the team is delighted to give players a new map, bringing back the compact setting of Flashpoint infused with the nation variety available on Battlegrounds USA. In total, the map offers 40 playable nations - a marked increase from Flashpoint’s 30. 

In both our internal and community feedback it was clear that America and Eastern nations did not have the dynamics that we’ve come to expect in high intensity compact maps - and with the great results of Battleground USA we were able to put said results into refreshing Flashpoint, including a new name: Western Theater.

For the time-being you will find Flashpoint in the map rotation still, but we will be adding Western Theater into the mix. As always, we welcome player feedback which can be shared on our discord.gg/con or forum.conflictnations.com

notes.notes:
+ + + + GENERAL UPDATE + + + +

Commanders,

While the team is working both on staying healthy as well as the mobile client. We are also improving our desktop version of Conflict of Nations. Today’s patch brings you among others some updated maps, tweaks to the UI, and server stability fixes. After a lengthy observation period, Rising Tides is receiving updates to its starting unit setup and AI. We believe stability already has improved substantially over the last days, but in light of the mobile release moving ever closer, we want to make sure that our systems are full-on ready to receive.

Speaking of maps, we’ve observed and discussed with the community at length about the required changes to our Rising Tides scenario. One big issue we found was the high level starting units causing more harm than good - something several of our players rightfully commented on. Also the AI was deemed to aggressive and disrupting.

After a lengthy observation period, Rising Tides is receiving updates to its starting unit setup and AI:
[list]    [*]The levels of starting units have been streamlined with other maps and rolled back to level 1. With this step we hope to reduce churn in early game, owing to the fact that losing your starting units left a significant power gap that could not be matched by ramping up new unit production.[/*]    [*]In line with this measure, we’ve also reduced The Chosen’s overall stats, with emphasis on their defensive capabilities. While we want The Chosen to pose a challenge and add to the chaos of Rising Tides, we never intended for them to absolutely dominate the map. With today’s changes they should still pose a threat when on the offensive, but claiming back your territory should now present less of an obstacle.[/*]    [*]IMPORTANT: Keep in mind these changes only apply to games spawned after the update.[/*][/list]
About the ramp-up: As you may have noticed, our community has grown significantly over the last few weeks! To cope with the demand, our devs have been working hard behind the scenes wrestling with servers, adding new servers, and identifying bottlenecks. If you’re experiencing disruptions in any of your games please don’t hesitate to reach out to us on any of our official channels!

Lastly, while mobile development enters it's critical phase, our map designers are currently busy putting the finishing touches on the overhauled Overkill map. You can expect it very soon™ on a PC near you.

In the meantime we hope you all stay healthy, and wish you luck on the battlefield!
